customer_persona: An everyday buyer exploring a compact SUV, with no individual priorities supplied yet. Offer a concrete cabin-led tour, then adapt only to what the customer actually says.
decision_frame: The strongest fit is a buyer who wants to compare available cabin equipment and rear-seat flexibility; the exact trim, personal seating fit and written on-road quote still need checking.
takeaway: Start with the cabin and flexible rear seats, then choose the trim with the equipment you want.
primary_outcome: Shortlist a CRETA trim by the cabin, seating and driving choices that matter to the buyer.
supporting_outcomes: Separate equipment shared across trims from the extras that change the choice.
Know which personal checks and written terms remain before booking.

concerns.why: Which of the visible cabin features actually belongs to the trim being considered?
How can the rear seat be arranged, and what still needs a personal luggage and seating check?
Which safety equipment is standard and which assistance features depend on trim or transmission?
Which engine and gearbox pairings are available without assuming driving feel or fuel economy?
The chosen trim needs a current written quote and its applicable warranty terms.

usps.name: Choose the cabin you want
usps.why_it_matters: A panoramic roof and ventilated front seats are concrete equipment choices to compare on the named trims, without promising an individual comfort result.

usps.name: Make room for changing plans
usps.why_it_matters: The split rear seat changes the passenger-and-luggage arrangement; selected trims also offer a reclining rear seat, while exact luggage volume remains unverified.

usps.name: Know what comes as standard
usps.why_it_matters: Six airbags and ISOFIX anchoring are listed across trims, so the buyer can distinguish standard equipment from trim-specific driver assistance.

segments.title: Inside the CRETA
segments.goal: MOMENT: start beside the pictured front seats and look up at the glass roof, inviting exploration rather than assigning a routine. SPOKEN: name the available panoramic roof and ventilated front seats from F247/F063 with selected-higher-trim qualification; save exact trim lists for deeper detail and make no cooling or comfort promise. VISUAL / HANDOFF: im05 shows seats and roof, im01 isolates the roof; ventilation is cited equipment, not visually demonstrated; leave attention on which cabin equipment matters, budget 26-32 words, no check-in.

segments.title: Cabin, space and standard equipment
segments.goal: MOMENT: turn the cabin opening into a short map of the choices, not another greeting or parts inventory. SPOKEN: summarize the three USPs as cabin choice, rear-seat flexibility and standard safety, using F247/F063, F096 and F237/F214; keep named-trim extras qualified and invite steering as a statement. VISUAL / HANDOFF: im05 cabin, im08 split seat and im09 airbag illustration in that order; carry the buyer into the feature they care about, budget 25-32 words, no question.
segments.outcome: Choose where to look more closely

segments.title: The seat and the glass roof
segments.goal: MOMENT: if the cabin catches the buyer's eye, inspect the roof opening before returning to the front seats. SPOKEN: F247 panoramic roof and F063 ventilated front seats on selected higher trims, naming SX Premium and King as shared examples only if useful; DEEPER: preserve exact F247 roof types and E/EX absence, exact F063 ventilation list/absence, and F159 manual versus dual-zone climate by trim. VISUAL / HANDOFF: im01 roof opening, im05 front seats, im03 climate controls only when discussing climate; no demonstrated ventilation or claimed thermal result; leave attention on the chosen seat and trim, budget 34-38 words, optional readiness check-in here.
segments.outcome: Compare the cabin equipment by trim

segments.title: When the rear seat folds
segments.goal: MOMENT: when people and bags share a trip, notice the pictured split seat with one part folded. SPOKEN: F096 split rear-seat arrangement, then F097 recline on selected trims; keep the split ratio and recline-step count in DEEPER with F032 seating count and an honest missing boot-volume/measurement-basis limit. VISUAL / HANDOFF: im08 proves the split arrangement, im06 shows the bench and im07 illustrates luggage only; never infer litres or guaranteed fit from bags in a photograph; leave attention on what the buyer would load, budget 31-36 words, no check-in.

segments.title: The screen beside the wheel
segments.goal: MOMENT: from the driver's seat, notice the screen stretching beside the steering wheel. SPOKEN: F162/F165 distinguish the infotainment display and driver display shown on equipped higher trims, without a usability or reduced-distraction promise; DEEPER: exact display sizes and named trims, including E having no standard infotainment screen. VISUAL / HANDOFF: im04 literally shows the two display areas and wheel; leave attention on the controls the buyer would try, budget 27-32 words, no check-in.

segments.title: Choosing the gearbox
segments.goal: MOMENT: before choosing a version to drive, separate the engine choice from the gearbox pairing. SPOKEN: petrol and diesel choices, with gearbox availability depending on the engine and trim; make clear the turbo petrol is automatic-only using F225/F229/F233, not a blanket each-engine choice. DEEPER / VISUAL / HANDOFF: retain all three exact engine-and-gearbox pairings and their full terminology; im02 is vehicle context only, not engine or driving-performance proof, and the literal engine/gearbox visual is a recorded gap; leave attention on the version to test, budget 31-36 words, no check-in.
segments.outcome: Choose an engine and gearbox pairing

segments.title: What comes across the range
segments.goal: MOMENT: when comparing trims, distinguish standard safety equipment from the additional assistance package. SPOKEN: F237 six airbags across trims, then F214 ISOFIX child-seat anchors; DEEPER: F153 named King/King Knight/Lounge assistance fitment and F154 automatic-transmission-only Smart Cruise Control, with no crash-proof or self-driving claim. VISUAL / HANDOFF: im09 is an airbag illustration only, not crash-test evidence or an ISOFIX/assistance demonstration; record those missing detail shots, leave attention on standard versus optional equipment, budget 30-36 words, optional readiness check-in here.
segments.outcome: Separate standard safety from trim extras

segments.title: Music and connected features
segments.goal: MOMENT: end the equipment tour with the things the buyer might choose to use between journeys. SPOKEN: F164 Bose audio on named higher trims and F168 Bluelink connected features with over-the-air updates on equipped trims; name Alexa only with the separately purchased Echo requirement in the same thought. DEEPER / VISUAL / HANDOFF: F243 three-year subscription and exact eligibility, F164 speaker count, F168 device purchase and named trim list; im10 shows speaker positions and im04 is display context rather than proof of an app or update, leave attention on which extras merit the trim, budget 30-38 words, no check-in.

segments.title: Before choosing your version
segments.goal: MOMENT: turn the shortlist into the details that must be settled before a purchase. SPOKEN: request the exact trim's written on-road quote and applicable warranty terms, and name unverified fuel-economy figures/test basis; DEEPER: F031 saved base ex-showroom price with exclusions, not a fresh quote, and F245 up-to-seven-year extension only for petrol on a payable basis, never standard coverage. VISUAL / HANDOFF: im02 identifies the car only, not prices or contracts; missing quote/warranty documents are gaps, the dealer supplies the written quote and terms while an official specification supplies economy/basis, budget 32-36 words, no check-in.
segments.outcome: Resolve price and written ownership terms

voice.persona_description: The guide notices concrete details and helps the buyer compare the choices. The guide is attentive, clear about limitations and unhurried when explaining trim differences.
voice.tone: Warm, cheerful and specific, with restrained enthusiasm and no pressure.

do_not_recommend_if: Do not recommend a trim until a feature the buyer requires is confirmed on that exact trim and their personal fit or written-price concern is resolved.
advance: After the buyer has a shortlist, select Book a Test Drive to request a drive and try the seating and controls; the dealer confirms the exact variant, written quote and appointment rather than treating the click as completed booking.
